session.objective:
Critique the VISUAL DESIGN of Aesop Studio and settle the open questions: the empty-state link colour (mint vs neutral), zebra vs separators, and whether a light theme belongs in the next release.
Facts about the current UI (from the design contract, 49 QA screenshots at 7 viewports, and a paid visual review):
- Theme "Coal / Ember", dark only: canvas #0B111A, panels #141F2C, raised #243243, hairline borders #2B3B4D,
  text #EEF4FA / #AFBED0, one coral primary action #FF916C (dark text), mint #80E1CB for verified, sky focus #9BD7FF.
  Segoe UI Variable; 14px body, 22px workspace heading; 12px panel radius; subtle shadows.
- Layout: 60px topbar (logo, breadcrumb Project / Workspace / Activity, Ctrl+K search, provider+route chip, help,
  inspector toggle), 64-68px icon+label rail (Chat, Build, Research, Memory, Saved; Providers/Evidence at bottom),
  220-248px project explorer with initials avatars and a coral 'New project' button, flexible canvas, 320-400px
  inspector with tabs Preview/Files/Changes/Terminal/Logs. Mobile: bottom nav, one column.
- Chat: message cards with avatar initials, provider name + access-route chip + status pill, cost line for metered
  calls; composer card with attachment chips, Ctrl+Enter hint, 'Preview context' and a coral Send.
- Research: two-column forms (Add a source / Record a finding), proposals in dashed sky cards.
- Evidence: KPI tiles for budget, tables for acceptance/latency/research.
- QA status: 0 horizontal overflow at 360-1920px, all controls >=40px, WCAG text contrast 5.9-17:1.
- Known weaknesses: the project header block (title, root path chip, provider chips, Settings) repeats the topbar and
  takes ~170px before content; two coral buttons can be visible at once (New project + Send/Start); dark-only;
  dense metadata chips; tables are plain; empty states are text-heavy; no light theme or brand illustration.
session.deliverable: a decision on each open question with the reasoning and dissent

# Roundtable decision memo

_Synthesized by Claude Code (participant) from the transcript. Votes are advisory._

# Aesop Studio visual design decision memo

Roundtable of 2026-10-23. Speakers: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor. Votes are advisory and confer no authority.

## Best-supported proposal

All three speakers converged on the same three answers by close. Reasoning is attributed per speaker below.

- **Empty-state links: neutral, not mint.** Secondary text colour, underlined, sky colour on hover and focus. Claude Code and Codex held this from their openings. Cursor opened with a mint dissent and withdrew it after Claude Code's reply. The shared reason is that mint is contract-bound to "verified", so a mint link teaches a false status semantic and adds a third accent beside coral and sky.
- **Tables: hairline separators, not zebra.** All three preferred separators from the start. Codex and Cursor argued zebra adds weight and fights the dense chips already in view. Cursor added that zebra makes Evidence blocks look like a spreadsheet export. The final zebra trigger is observed row misreads in Evidence tasks, not a column count.
- **Light theme: not in the next release.** All three agreed. The shared basis is evidence priority: the paid review already flagged the repeated project header and dual coral buttons, and those fixes come first. Cost arguments were partly withdrawn, as noted under Direct exchanges.

A fourth rule emerged that nobody opened with. **Single-coral discipline**: New project is neutral inside workspaces and coral only in the project-creation empty state. Codex proposed the split, Claude Code adopted it, Cursor endorsed it. Codex and Cursor still differ on the exact trigger, covered under Dissent.

| Token | Final role |
|---|---|
| #AFBED0 | Empty-state link text, underlined |
| #9BD7FF | Link hover and focus |
| #80E1CB | Verified status only |
| #2B3B4D | Table row separators |
| #FF916C | One primary action per view |

## Competing recommendations

- **Mint for success-path empty-state CTAs** (Cursor, opening). Withdrawn.
- **Six-column zebra trigger at 1280px** (Claude Code). Withdrawn after Codex called it arbitrary.
- **Canvas brightness step as the glare remedy** (Claude Code). Codex rejected it as an untested hypothesis. Not adopted.
- **Scoped paper surface in the inspector Preview tab** (Cursor). Codex said it cannot address Chat or Evidence discomfort and must be tested first. Not adopted; left as a follow-up.
- **Dashed sky frames around empty states** (Cursor). Claude Code and Codex both objected that they borrow Research's proposal grammar. Not adopted.
- **Taller Evidence rows, roughly 40px minimum** (Cursor). Not contested, not formally adopted.

## Evidence cited

- Design contract reserving mint for verified: Claude Code [E2], Codex [E3], Cursor [E4].
- Paid review weaknesses, the repeated header and dual coral CTAs: Claude Code [E2], Codex [E3], Cursor [E4].
- Three-tier surface system and dense chips as a reason against zebra: Claude Code [E2], Cursor [E4], Codex [E7].
- 49 screenshots at 7 viewports as a QA cost: Claude Code [E2], Cursor [E4], corrected by Codex [E7] and conceded by Claude Code [E9].
- Codex stated repeatedly that nobody in the room inspected the screenshots or tested readability [E3], [E7], [E10], [E12], [E16].

## Dissent

- **Codex on the coral trigger.** Coral eligibility should follow the primary task, not a zero-projects count. Returning users may still be creating a project [E12], [E16]. Cursor and Claude Code settled on zero projects [E13], [E15].
- **Codex on light mode.** Deferral is pending readability evidence, not a settled no. Reported glare or reading difficulty should move it up [E3], [E10].
- **Cursor on Preview paper.** Still wants it as a scoped readability hatch and says it does not replace glare testing [E17]. Codex wants it tested before any commitment [E12].
- **Cursor on dashed sky frames.** Still wants them [E11]. Claude Code and Codex oppose them [E12], [E15].
- **Codex on separators.** Separator visibility against the panel colours is unverified and may need adjustment [E7], [E16].

## Unresolved risks

- No participant looked at the 49 screenshots. Every colour and spacing claim rests on hex values and the review summary.
- Separator contrast against panel surfaces was never measured.
- No user readability data exists for the dark theme, so the glare question is open.
- The zebra trigger depends on observing Evidence misreads, and no observation method was defined.
- The New project rule has two live definitions, zero projects versus primary task, and the implementer must pick one.

## Direct exchanges

- **Claude Code to Codex [E5].** Proposed a brightness step and a six-column zebra trigger. Codex rejected both in [E10] as arbitrary and untested. Claude Code withdrew the trigger in [E15].
- **Claude Code to Cursor [E6].** Argued mint CTAs reopen the two-coral problem. Cursor conceded in [E11] and dropped mint entirely.
- **Codex to Claude Code [E7].** Said zebra needs no fourth surface and light mode does not double QA. Claude Code conceded both cost points in [E9] and said the decision rests on evidence priority instead. Claude Code also adopted Codex's New project split.
- **Cursor to Codex and Claude Code [E8].** Proposed Preview paper, dashed frames, and 40px rows. Codex answered in [E12] that paper cannot fix Chat or Evidence and frames risk confusion with proposals.
- **Codex to Cursor [E12] and Cursor back [E13].** Cursor reframed paper as a scoped hatch and kept it. Codex kept the task-based coral rule.

## Follow-ups

1. Collapse the roughly 170px project header so it stops repeating the topbar.
2. Make New project secondary inside workspaces and pick one coral trigger definition.
3. Shorten empty-state copy; one coral action, neutral links for the rest.
4. Measure separator contrast on the panel and canvas colours and adjust the hairline if needed.
5. Define how Evidence row misreads will be observed before any zebra trial.
6. Gather user readability feedback on the dark theme before the following release's theme decision.
7. Prototype the inspector Preview paper surface as a test, not a commitment.

## Conditions for implementation

- Mint appears nowhere except verified status.
- Exactly one coral control is visible per view in the common case.
- Link hover and focus use the sky token so focus stays consistent with the rest of the UI.
- Separators remain the default. Zebra is only trialled after recorded misreads.
- No global light theme work starts until the header collapse and single-coral rule ship.
- Any paper surface or dashed frame ships only after a screenshot and readability check, which nobody in this session performed.

## Provenance and consumption

- Codex via `codex`: 5 accepted turn(s), last latency 15.03s, cost $0.000000, final state idle
- Claude Code via `claude`: 5 accepted turn(s), last latency 11.52s, cost $0.000000, final state idle
- Cursor via `cursor`: 5 accepted turn(s), last latency 17.79s, cost $0.000000, final state idle

## Coverage

3 of 3 approved speakers contributed (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor). Valid three-administrator War Room: yes.

events.label: E2
events.speaker: claude
events.content:
Opening position, independent of the other participants.

**Empty-state link colour:** neutral text #AFBED0 with underline, not mint. Mint is contractually reserved for "verified". Reusing it for links teaches users a false semantic. Links in empty states are secondary prompts, not status.

**Zebra vs separators:** hairline separators #2B3B4D. Zebra on a dark palette needs a fourth surface tone, which crowds the three-tier canvas/panel/raised system and fights the dense chips already present. Separators plus row hover is enough.

**Light theme:** no, not next release. The bigger visible defects are the ~170px repeated project header and two simultaneous coral primaries. Fix those first. A light theme doubles contrast QA across 49 screenshots for an unproven demand.

POSITION: Neutral links, hairline separators, defer light theme and spend the release on header collapse and single-primary discipline.

events.label: E3
events.speaker: openai
events.content:
The visual hierarchy needs work before another theme: collapse the ~170px project header, reduce metadata chips, and make New project secondary so Send/Start owns coral.

- **Empty-state links: neutral**, underlined with sky focus. Reserve mint for verified status; navigation should not imply verification.
- **Tables: separators**, restrained headers, and generous row spacing. Zebra striping adds visual weight; reconsider only if dense, wide tables prove difficult to track.
- **Light theme: defer next release.** Fix hierarchy and empty-state brevity first. Dissent: light mode deserves priority if users report glare or difficulty reading dark surfaces.

I have not inspected screenshots; contrast scores alone cannot establish visual clarity.

POSITION: Choose neutral links and separators, and defer light mode while repairing hierarchy.

events.label: E4
events.speaker: cursor
events.content:

**Empty-state links:** Use **neutral secondary text (#AFBED0) with sky focus (#9BD7FF) on hover/focus**, not mint. Mint is already contract-bound to *verified*; mint links in sparse empty states read like “already done” and add a third accent beside coral and sky. Dissent: mint could lift morale in dead canvases—only if links are strictly “success-path” CTAs, not generic “learn more.”

**Tables:** **Hairline row separators** (#2B3B4D), not zebra. On #141F2C/#0B111A, zebra fights panel elevation and makes Evidence KPI + table blocks feel like spreadsheet export, not Coal/Ember. Separators match existing borders and survive dense metadata chips.

**Light theme:** **Not next release.** Ship visual debt fixes first (shrink ~170px project header, resolve dual coral CTAs, lighten empty states). A light theme doubles the 49-viewport matrix without fixing the weaknesses the review already flagged.

**POSITION:** Neutral+sky empty-state links, separator tables, defer light theme until hierarchy and single-primary-CTA rules land.

events.label: E5
events.speaker: claude
events.content:
@Codex [E3] we agree on all three, so let me sharpen your dissent. "Users report glare" is not a trigger for a full light theme. The cheaper answer is a canvas brightness step, keeping the three surface tiers. Also, Evidence tables are already wide and dense. Set a concrete zebra trigger now: adopt it only if the latency table exceeds six columns at 1280px. Otherwise we revisit forever.

POSITION: Neutral links, separators with a measurable zebra trigger, defer light theme and answer glare with a brightness step, not a second palette.

events.label: E6
events.speaker: claude
events.content:
@Cursor [E4] your dissent, mint for "success-path" empty-state CTAs, reopens the two-coral problem through a side door. An empty canvas has one real action: start something. That is coral, once. Everything else is neutral. A mint CTA becomes a third accent competing with coral and sky, exactly what you argued against for tables. Concede instead: the morale lift comes from a single coral button plus shorter copy, not a new link colour.

POSITION: Neutral links, one coral CTA per empty state, separators, defer light theme.

events.label: E7
events.speaker: openai

events.content:

Tables: hairlines plus **40px min row height** in Evidence. POSITION: Neutral links, separator tables with taller rows, defer global light theme; allow inspector Preview paper only.

events.content:
@Codex [E7] conceded on cost: zebra can reuse #141F2C on #0B111A rows, and light-mode QA is nearer 7 viewports times a contrast pass, not 49 new captures. The decision holds on evidence priority, not cost. Your New-project split is better than mine: neutral in workspaces, coral only in the empty project-creation state. Adopt it as the single-primary rule.

POSITION: Neutral links, separators, defer light theme, and New project is coral only when no project exists.

events.label: E10
events.speaker: openai

events.label: E11
events.speaker: cursor
events.content:
@Claude on [E6]: Concede—drop mint for empty-state links and CTAs. One coral action per empty canvas; other prompts stay neutral #AFBED0, underlined, sky focus. Morale is shorter copy plus illustration later, not a third accent. I still want dashed sky frames [E8] for hierarchy without implying verified.

POSITION: Neutral links only, single coral empty-state CTA, hairline separators, defer global light theme.

events.speaker: openai

events.content:

Inspector Preview paper [E8] is a scoped hatch, not “light theme”; still defer any global palette until header collapse and single-coral land. @Claude [E9]: Neutral links only; coral **New project** only when zero projects exist.

POSITION: Neutral links, hairline separators, zebra only after proven tracking failures, defer global light theme next release.

events.label: E14
events.content: Open floor closed. Closing statements.

events.label: E15
events.speaker: claude
events.content:
Final: neutral underlined links with sky focus, hairline separators, defer light theme. Changed my mind twice: Codex's New-project split (neutral in workspaces, coral only with zero projects) replaces mine, and I withdrew the six-column zebra trigger for observed Evidence row misreads. Still disagree with Cursor's dashed sky frames for empty states, since they borrow Research's proposal grammar.

POSITION: Neutral links, separators, zebra only after proven misreads, light theme deferred behind header collapse and single-coral discipline.

events.label: E16
events.speaker: openai
events.content:
Recommend neutral underlined links with sky focus, separators, and deferring light mode. I refined the coral rule: New project becomes secondary inside workspaces. My remaining disagreement: coral eligibility should follow the primary task, not whether users have zero projects; returning users can prioritize project creation.

Screenshots and readability remain unchecked; separators may need adjustment.

POSITION: Choose neutral links, separator tables, and defer light mode pending readability evidence.
